tldr: Scored against our full 25-criteria rubric, these two are close — both are genuinely strong, well-integrated platforms — but Zendesk pulls slightly ahead on automation depth and sentiment/intent detection, while Intercom is more transparent about what AI resolutions actually cost.

Intercom is cheaper to start ($29/seat/mo) and its Fin AI agent can be deployed onto an existing helpdesk without migrating seats; Zendesk doesn't unlock AI Agents until the $55/agent/mo Suite Team tier.

Both vendors' AI-resolution marketing claims are inflated relative to independent reporting: Intercom cites ~70-76% resolution against an independently-reported real-world range of roughly 38-80% depending on knowledge-base quality, and Zendesk cites '80%+' against independent write-ups describing 10-20% in fresh deployments, climbing toward 70% only in mature, heavily-curated setups.

Zendesk's Action Builder supports true multi-step agentic workflows (up to 50 steps, branching conditions) and its Intelligent Triage auto-classifies sentiment and intent on every ticket — both score a full 5/5 here, edging out Intercom's workflow-engine-based automation and CX Score sentiment tool.

Pricing transparency actually favors Intercom: it publishes its $0.99-per-resolution AI fee outright, while Zendesk doesn't disclose its per-resolution rate at all — third-party trackers estimate $1.50-$2.00 per resolution, and that undisclosed, stacking AI meter is the single most-repeated complaint in independent Zendesk reviews.

Pick Intercom for a faster AI-first deployment with slightly better cost predictability; pick Zendesk if you need the deepest ticket routing and workflow automation and can absorb a steeper learning curve and less transparent AI billing.
verdict: This comes down to how fast you need to move and how much workflow depth you actually need, because on raw capability these two are closer than either vendor's marketing would suggest. Intercom's standalone Fin deployment lets you test AI resolution quality against your existing helpdesk before committing to anything, and it's the more transparent one on AI cost — $0.99 per resolution is a number you can actually build a forecast around. Zendesk asks for more up front (you're not touching AI Agents until $55/agent/mo, a full $26 more per seat than Intercom's entry price) and it doesn't publish its per-resolution AI rate at all — third-party trackers put it around $1.50-$2.00, and that opacity is the single most-repeated complaint in independent Zendesk reviews. What you get for that is real, though: Zendesk's Action Builder does genuine multi-step agentic workflows up to 50 steps deep, and Intelligent Triage auto-scores sentiment and intent on every incoming ticket without extra configuration — both score a clean 5/5 in our rubric, ahead of Intercom's respectable but slightly less deep equivalents. Neither company's AI-resolution number should be trusted at face value: Intercom's 70-76% claim and Zendesk's '80%+' claim both sit well above what independent reporting actually finds once you're past a narrow, well-documented FAQ set, which is why both score a conservative 3/5 on that specific criterion in our rubric rather than the 4s or 5s their marketing pages would suggest. My honest read: choose Intercom if you want to move fast and know your AI costs upfront; choose Zendesk if deep ticket routing and workflow automation matter more to you than pricing transparency, and budget extra headroom for the AI line item regardless of which you pick.
